skill.name: move-code-quality
skill.description: Reviews Move packages against the Move Book Code Quality Checklist, including Move 2024 syntax, manifests, functions, tests, documentation, and Sui conventions.
skill.summary: Review Move packages for modern syntax, package configuration, composability, testing, and documentation quality.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 102 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, Move macro names, ordinary review prose, and a documentation URL. SKILL.md contains guidance only and does not execute commands, construct dynamic functions, perform reconnaissance, or make network requests. No prompt injection or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Working in a directory containing `.move` files or `Move.toml`
- Find all `.move` files using glob patterns
- ✅ GOOD when importing members: `use my_package::my_module::{Self, Member};`
- ❌ BAD: `const NOT_AUTHORIZED: u64 = 0;` (all-caps reserved for regular constants)
- ❌ BAD: `const MyConstant: vector<u8> = b"value";` (PascalCase suggests error)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct AdminCap has key, store { id: UID }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct Admin has key, store { id: UID }` (unclear it's a capability)
- ❌ BAD: `public struct PromisePotato {}` (redundant, abilities show it's hot potato)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct UserRegistered has copy, drop { user: address }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct RegisterUser has copy, drop { user: address }` (ambiguous)
- ✅ CANONICAL: `public struct DynamicFieldKey() has copy, drop, store;`
- ⚠️ ACCEPTABLE: `public struct DynamicField has copy, drop, store {}`
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun do_something(): T { ... }` (composable, returns value)
- ❌ BAD: `public fun mint_and_transfer(ctx: &mut TxContext) { transfer::transfer(...) }` (not compos
- ❌ BAD: `public fun authorize(cap: &AdminCap, app: &mut App)` (breaks method associativity)
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun details_mut(u: &mut User): &mut Details` (mutable accessor)
- ❌ BAD: `use std::string::utf8; let str = utf8(b"hello, world!");`
- ❌ BAD: `let mut my_vec = vector::empty(); vector::push_back(&mut my_vec, 10);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let sum = source.fold!(0, |acc, v| acc + v);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let filtered = source.filter!(|e| e > 10);` (requires T: drop)
- ❌ BAD: `let MyStruct { id, field_1: _, field_2: _, field_3: _ } = value;`
- ❌ BAD: Separate `#[test]` and `#[expected_failure]` on different lines
- ✅ GOOD: End with `abort` to show failure point
- ❌ BAD: Include `test.end()` or other cleanup in expected_failure tests
- ❌ BAD: `#[test] fun test_this_feature() { }` (redundant in test module)
- ✅ GOOD for simple tests: `let ctx = &mut tx_context::dummy();`
- ❌ BAD: `assert!(is_success, 0);` (may conflict with app error codes)
- ✅ GOOD: `assert_eq!(result, expected_value);` (shows both values on failure)
- **Testing** - Use simplest approach that works; avoid over-engineering

content.user_title: Review Move Code Against Modern Quality Standards
content.value_statement: Move projects can drift from modern syntax and package conventions. This skill reviews Move packages against the Move Book checklist and returns prioritized, actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Discovers Move.toml files, Move source files, and test modules within the requested package scope.
Checks Move.toml edition settings, framework dependencies, and named address prefixes.
Reviews module syntax, imports, constants, structs, function signatures, and parameter ordering.
Evaluates modern Move methods, option macros, loop macros, vector usage, and collection access patterns.
Reviews test attributes, naming, assertions, cleanup, and TestScenario usage.
Produces prioritized findings with file locations, impact explanations, and recommended changes.
limitations: Provides checklist-based quality guidance, not a formal smart contract security audit.
Recommendations assume Move 2024 and modern Sui conventions, which may not fit older packages.
Cannot verify compilation, tests, or formatter output unless the required tools are available and executed.
Automatic fixes require user approval and should be reviewed before deployment.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Move Package
use_cases.description: Find legacy syntax, manifest settings, and API patterns that should change for Move 2024.

use_cases.title: Review a Move Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check changed modules for naming, composability, parameter ordering, and current Sui conventions.

use_cases.title: Improve Move Tests
use_cases.description: Identify unnecessary scenarios, weak assertions, outdated attributes, and cleanup patterns in test modules.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Move File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [file path] against the Move 2024 code quality checklist. Report prioritized findings with line numbers and concise fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants focused feedback on one module.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Move Manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Move.toml path] for edition settings, implicit framework dependencies, and named address prefixes. Explain each issue and suggest a correction.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a focused package configuration review.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Full Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the Move package at [directory]. Include source and test modules, group findings by severity, and identify patterns that already follow guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer wants a complete checklist review before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Move 2024 Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [package directory] with Move 2024 and Sui 1.45+ conventions. Prioritize migration work, note compatibility assumptions, and propose staged changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team is planning a package-wide migration.

output_examples.input: Review the package manifest and main source module for Move 2024 compliance.
output: Critical: Move.toml does not declare the Move 2024 edition. Add the edition before adopting checklist features.
Important: The main module uses legacy module syntax. Convert it to the modern module label format.
Passed: Named addresses use package-specific prefixes.

output_examples.input: Check the test module for maintainability.
output: Important: Expected-failure attributes are split across lines. Merge them for consistency.
Recommended: A simple context is sufficient for this test. Remove unnecessary scenario setup.
Passed: Assertions use comparison helpers that show both values on failure.

best_practices: Define the review scope and target Move or Sui version before analysis.
Review critical manifest and edition findings before style recommendations.
Validate suggested changes with the formatter, compiler, and tests before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not treat checklist compliance as proof of contract security.
Do not apply every recommendation without considering package version and compatibility.
Do not report vague findings without file locations, impact, and a concrete correction.

faq.question: Does this skill perform a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It reviews code quality conventions and may complement, but cannot replace, a dedicated smart contract security audit.

faq.question: Which Move versions does it target?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Move 2024 and modern Sui conventions, including dependency behavior introduced in Sui 1.45+.

faq.question: Can it review one file instead of a package?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a specific Move file, manifest, function, test, or checklist category.

faq.question: Can it fix findings automatically?
faq.answer: It can offer and apply changes when approved. Review and test every change before deployment.

faq.question: Does it compile or test the package?
faq.answer: Only when suitable tools are available and execution is requested. Otherwise, it performs a source-based review.

faq.question: What does the report include?
faq.answer: The report groups findings by priority and includes file locations, impact, recommended changes, and recognized good practices.
